title: Project state — v1.0
description: Chainlink #55/#56. The output contract for the future `ligature status --json`, specified here so #56 implements against a fixed shape rather than inventing one mid-build. This schema does not exist because #56 is implemented -- it is not; #56 remains the task that writes the code computing a document this schema can validate. Every enum in this schema that reports a checked condition also carries an explicit 'unknown'/'not-checked' member (never omitted, never collapsed into the nearest-looking pass value) so a status command that could not determine something reports that honestly instead of defaulting to clean. Witness/implementation OBSERVATIONS (what the code and its generated projections currently show) are kept in a separate `generated_observations` object from `assurance` (what is actually verified) everywhere this schema has both, per plan.md's own witness-vs-assurance discipline (G18/G19/G20, the feature ledger's implementation_observed vs assurance_status split) -- a status document that let a witness observation stand in for an assurance verdict would be exactly the conflation that discipline exists to prevent.

version.description: The running product's own version, e.g. from #57's `ligature version`. Distinct from schema_version above -- this document's own shape can outlive several product releases.

installation_manifest.description: #58's ownership manifest, read (not recomputed) by status. A workspace with no manifest at all is `not-initialized`, never silently reported as if every field below were clean.

installed_schema_versions.description: schema name -> installed version, e.g. {"project-state": "1.0"}. Empty object when not-initialized.

binary_identity.description: #57: the executable is the trusted adjudicator, not just the files it validated. `verified: unknown` is required (not `false`) when running from an unattested source checkout rather than a packaged build -- today's `python3 scripts/pipeline.py` invocation has no build hash to verify at all, which is a distinct state from 'verification ran and failed'.

generated_observations.description: Implementation-observed projections (feature ledger, contact sheet, witness renders) -- explicitly NOT assurance. Never read as a pass/fail verdict by anything consuming this document.

kind.description: One of docs/cli-contract.md §2's artifact-kind values, e.g. 'boundary', 'interaction', 'bridge'.

content_hash.description: Required (a real hash, never null) for every declared lifecycle except 'absent' -- including 'invalid' (an invalid file still hashes). 'absent' requires content_hash to be null (the file has no bytes to hash); 'unknown' permits either, honestly: lifecycle could not be determined, but the file may still have been readable and hashable independently of that determination. See the `allOf` conditionals below, which are what actually enforces this, not this description on its own.

lifecycle.description: 'unknown' is for a status run that could not determine lifecycle (e.g. a read error unrelated to the artifact's own validity) -- distinct from 'invalid', which means status COULD check it and it failed. 'stale-by-hash-drift' means a promoted artifact's on-disk content_hash no longer matches the hash recorded at promotion time.

promoted_hash.description: The hash recorded at promotion time, present whenever lifecycle is 'promoted' or 'stale-by-hash-drift' so the two can be compared without a second lookup. Required by the conditionals below whenever lifecycle is one of those two values; absent (the key not present at all) otherwise -- there is no promotion-time hash to report for a never-promoted or absent artifact.

allOf.description: lifecycle 'absent' <=> content_hash null. An absent artifact has no bytes to hash; every other declared lifecycle (including 'invalid') implies the file was read and does have a real hash.

promoted_hash is required (and non-null) exactly when lifecycle is 'promoted' or 'stale-by-hash-drift', and must be absent otherwise -- it does not exist to report for a lifecycle that was never promoted.

required_assurance.description: Every dimension this obligation's own reliance declares as required. Dimensions are never merged/deduped into a single boolean -- an obligation requiring both 'formal' and 'differential' assurance and achieving only one is NOT 'partially satisfied', it is two separate dimension records, one achieved and one not.

dimension.description: e.g. 'formal', 'differential', 'harness-tested', 'human-review' -- plan.md §8.1's claim/evidence/result/scope/trust/support split names the vocabulary; this schema does not close it since #56 owns the real enumeration -- EXCEPT for the one value schema-forbidden outright below. A prior revision only said 'witness' doesn't belong here in prose while the schema itself accepted any non-empty string, including literally 'witness' (external review, round 2: `{"dimension": "witness", "status": "achieved"}` validated with zero errors). `not: {const: witness}` makes that specific claim schema-rejected, not merely discouraged in a comment a future caller has no reason to read: a witness is a typed MITIGATION acceptable only at risk tier low (plan.md §16), never itself an assurance dimension a stronger obligation can rely on achieving -- see generated_observations.witness_summaries, which is where a witness's own determinism/degeneracy observation lives, structurally separate from this array. The broader vocabulary stays open (no enum) since #56 owns closing it; only this one collision is closed here.

limitations.description: Free-text per docs/degradation-record-schema.json's failed_conditions when state is 'degraded' or 'blocked'; empty array (not omitted) when 'closes' or 'unknown'.

finding_ref.description: A lighter pointer than consolidated-check.schema.json's own finding shape -- status reports THAT a finding is open, check owns full provenance/authority detail for a given run. dedup_key must match the same identity scheme consolidated-check.schema.json's findings use so a finding referenced from both documents is recognizably the same finding.

witness_summary.description: generated_observations only -- these are witness/implementation observations (G19 determinism, G20 degeneracy), deliberately never an assurance_status field. plan.md §16.3's contact sheet keeps this traffic-light column visually distinct from a never-green assurance column for the same reason.
